ErrorResponse.description:
The body of every non-2xx response (SPEC §10, Appendix A.2).

`message` is written for the user and can be shown as it is. `details` is an
object, empty unless the code is one of these:

* `VALIDATION_ERROR`. A request that does not match its schema: `errors`, a list
  of `{loc, msg, type}`, one per field, the first 50 at most. `loc` ends with the
  name of the field, `msg` is a sentence for the person who filled it in, to be
  shown under the field as it is ("Use at most 200 characters."), and `type`
  names the rule that was broken. A body that is no JSON has one entry, whose
  `loc` begins with `body` and whose `type` is `json_invalid`. A rule a service
  checks: `field`, the name of the offending field, and `message` is the
  sentence for it. A profile created without `policy_accepted: true` is such a
  rule, and its `field` is `policy_accepted`; so is a filter of the leaderboard
  whose `min_…` is above its `max_…`, with the `min_…` as its `field`.
* `FORBIDDEN`, when the portal's id is not an address MarkETH is open to:
  `allowed_domains`, a list of the domains it is open to.
* `PROFILE_REQUIRED`: `name` and `email`, who the portal says is calling. `name`
  may be an empty string.
* `USERNAME_TAKEN`: `field`, which is `username`.
* `RATE_LIMITED`: `retry_after_seconds`, an integer, also sent as the
  `Retry-After` header.
* `QUOTE_STALE`: `quote`, a fresh `QuoteResponse` for the same trade.
* `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`: `limit`, which names the limit: `MAX_STAKE_PER_USER_MARKET`,
  `MAX_PROPOSALS_PER_USER_PER_DAY`, `MAX_OPEN_MARKETS`, `MAX_MARKET_BUDGET`,
  `MAX_AGGREGATE_LOSS_BUDGET`, `MAX_CODE_ISSUANCE_PER_MONTH`,
  `ONE_CODE_PER_USER` or `MAX_ADMIN_ADJUSTMENT_CR`. With
  `MAX_STAKE_PER_USER_MARKET` also `stake_limit_cr`, `stake_left_cr` and
  `required_cr`, what the buy costs; with `MAX_CODE_ISSUANCE_PER_MONTH` also
  `issued_cr`, `requested_cr` and `cap_cr`; with `MAX_ADMIN_ADJUSTMENT_CR` also
  `requested_cr`, what the adjustment would add, and `cap_cr`, the most one
  adjustment may add.
* `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`: `balance_cr` and `required_cr`. Where an admin debits
  somebody's balance, they are what that account holds and what the debit takes.
* `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, from `GET /health` only: `postgres`, `redis` and
  `scylla`, each `up` or `down`.

A quote is answered like its trade. `GET /markets/{id}/quote` gives a buy the
caller could not make the error the trade would get, with the same message and
details: `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` with `MAX_STAKE_PER_USER_MARKET`, `stake_limit_cr`,
`stake_left_cr` and `required_cr` above the stake left, `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`
with `balance_cr` and `required_cr` above the balance.

Amounts in `details` are decimal strings like every `*_cr` field.
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

ProposeMarketRequest.description:
`POST /markets`: what a proposal must state (SPEC §6).

The time rules that depend on the clock are the service's: `close_at` in the future
and within `MAX_MARKET_LIFETIME`, `resolve_by` within `MAX_RESOLUTION_DELAY_DAYS`
of `close_at`.

A proposal says nothing about liquidity: the admin who approves the market picks
its tier. A field that names one is refused like any field the request does not
have.

QuoteResponse.description:
What a trade would do right now. Also sent as `details.quote` of `QUOTE_STALE`.

`GET /markets/{id}/quote` answers with it for a trade the caller could make. For
one they could not, it answers the error the trade would get instead, with the
same code, message and details: 403 `FORBIDDEN` in a market the caller proposed,
409 `MARKET_NOT_OPEN`, 409 `INSUFFICIENT_SHARES` for a sell of more than the
caller holds, 422 `TRADE_TOO_SMALL`, 409 `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` for a buy above the
stake left and 409 `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE` for one above the balance. So the
answer to a typed amount is the server's, and the client compares nothing.

The client cuts the code out of the query, in the wallet page a phone camera opens
and in the in-app scanner alike, and sends only that. A whole URL is not a code: it

portal.description: The request header in which the portal names the caller after ETH single sign-on. The portal adds it on the way to the API; a client of this API never sends it. Its name is the server's IDENTITY_HEADER_USER_ID setting. The list of an operation says what the caller needs beyond being named: `REGISTERED` is a saved profile, `BARISTA` and `ADMIN` are roles. A suspended account is refused wherever an identity is needed.
portal.name: X-User-Id

info.description:
Everything sits under `/api`, on the same origin as the app. There is no sign-in here: the portal in front of the API signs a person in and names them in a request header.

* Credits (`*_cr`) and shares are decimal strings with at most six places, never JSON numbers. Probabilities are numbers in [0, 1], already rounded for display.
* Every error has one shape, `ErrorResponse`: switch on `code`, show `message`.
* Each operation says who may call it, in its description and in `security`.
* A request with a method other than GET, HEAD or OPTIONS must carry an `Origin` header the server allows, or it is answered with 403 `FORBIDDEN`.
info.title: MarkETH API
